items.q: Do I need prior pottery experience?
items.a: Not at all. Our weekend workshops welcome complete beginners. We teach foundational techniques step-by-step in small, supportive groups.

items.q: What can I make in one workshop?

items.q: How many people attend each class?
items.a: We keep groups to 6 students maximum, ensuring hands-on instruction and individual attention throughout the weekend session.

items.q: When are workshops scheduled?
items.a: Workshops run most weekends year-round. Check our calendar for dates and book at least two weeks in advance for availability.

content.ctaBody: Join our next weekend workshop and discover the meditative art of traditional Japanese pottery.

features.title: Weekend Classes
features.body: Small group sessions held Saturdays and Sundays, designed for both complete beginners and returning students seeking deeper practice.

features.title: Traditional Techniques
features.body: Master hand-throwing, coiling, and hand-building methods rooted in Kyoto's centuries-old ceramic heritage and philosophy.

features.title: Local Studio Space
features.body: Work in our historic Kyoto studio surrounded by authentic kilns and tools, immersed in the atmosphere where pottery traditions were born.

features.title: Take Home Your Work
features.body: Fire and glaze your creations in our kilns. Each piece becomes a personal memory of your time learning in Kyoto's pottery heartland.

featuresDeep.title: Ancient Methods, Living Practice
featuresDeep.body: We teach the same hand-throwing and surface techniques that potters have refined across generations in Kyoto. Rather than shortcuts or industrial methods, you'll experience the tactile discipline and patience that defines authentic Japanese ceramics, connecting your hands directly to this living heritage.

featuresDeep.title: Intimate Group Setting
featuresDeep.body: Limited to small groups each weekend, ensuring personalized instruction and the quiet focus needed to truly connect with clay. You'll share the studio with fellow learners, creating a community around the meditative craft rather than a crowded classroom experience.

featuresDeep.title: Kyoto's Historic Context
featuresDeep.body: Our studio location places you in the heart of Kyoto's pottery district, where you can walk streets shaped by centuries of ceramic tradition. Learning here isn't just about technique—it's about absorbing the cultural weight and aesthetic sensibility that have always defined Kyoto clay work.

props.title: Find Us & Book
props.note: Workshops are by advance booking only. Parking available in nearby lot. Groups of 4+ welcome with prior arrangement.

items.q: Do I need prior pottery experience?
items.a: Not at all. Our weekend workshops welcome complete beginners. We teach foundational techniques step-by-step in small, supportive groups.

items.q: What can I make in one workshop?
items.a: Most students complete a hand-thrown bowl or simple vessel. Pieces are glazed and fired; we ship finished work internationally if needed.

items.q: How many people attend each class?
items.a: We keep groups to 6 students maximum, ensuring hands-on instruction and individual attention throughout the weekend session.

items.q: When are workshops scheduled?
items.a: Workshops run most weekends year-round. Check our calendar for dates and book at least two weeks in advance for availability.

props.note: Located in the artisan district of Kyoto, Japan. Weekend sessions year-round.
